title: Strings and JSON
summary: Clean up messy text, and query JSON stored in a column.

steps.title: Cleaning text
body: Larkspur is launching one loyalty programme across all its businesses, and the sign-up form let people type anything. Text functions to the rescue:
Dialects: SQL Server has `LEN`, `CHARINDEX`, `SUBSTRING`; PostgreSQL has `position('@' in s)`, `split_part`, and regular expressions; MySQL has `LOCATE` and `SUBSTRING_INDEX`.

setup: CREATE TABLE signups (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, raw_name TEXT, email TEXT, phone TEXT, meta TEXT);

INSERT INTO signups VALUES (1,'  ana SOUSA ','Ana.Sousa@Mail.test','+44 7700 900123','{"source":"web","tags":["books","theatre"],"marketing":true}'),(2,'Ben Okoro','ben@mail.test','07700-900456','{"source":"app","tags":["bikes"],"marketing":false}'),(3,'chloe park','CHLOE@MAIL.TEST ','(07700) 900789','{"source":"web","tags":[],"marketing":true}'),(4,'Dmitri  Volkov','dmitri@mail.test',NULL,'{"source":"box office","tags":["theatre","games"],"marketing":true,"referrer":"R-17"}'),(5,'esme hart','esme@mail.test','07700 900321','{"source":"app","tags":["games"],"marketing":false,"referrer":"R-17"}');
steps.explain: TRIM removes the trailing space, LOWER fixes the shouting, and everything after the `@` is the domain.

steps.title: JSON in a column
body: Some data doesn't fit fixed columns, so apps store **JSON** in a text column. SQLite's JSON functions read it:
SELECT meta ->> '$.source' FROM signups;                   -- same, shorter (SQLite 3.38+)
SELECT json_extract(meta, '$.tags[0]') FROM signups;        -- first array element
`json_each` turns a JSON array into **rows** you can join, filter and group:
FROM signups AS s, json_each(s.meta, '$.tags') AS t;
PostgreSQL: `meta->>'source'` on a `jsonb` column (indexable with GIN). SQL Server: `JSON_VALUE(meta, '$.source')` and `OPENJSON`. MySQL: `meta->>'$.source'`.

setup: CREATE TABLE signups (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, raw_name TEXT, email TEXT, phone TEXT, meta TEXT);

steps.explain: `->>` returns the value as plain SQL text; `json_array_length` counts the tags array.

steps.title: Where sign-ups come from
prompt: Return each **source** (from the JSON) and how many sign-ups came from it (**signups**).
Tables: `signups(id, raw_name, email, phone, meta)`; `meta` is JSON text such as `{"source":"web","tags":["books"],"marketing":true}`.
solution: SELECT meta ->> '$.source' AS source, COUNT(*) AS signups
setup: CREATE TABLE signups (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, raw_name TEXT, email TEXT, phone TEXT, meta TEXT);

steps.prompt: Complete the query: each tag and how many members chose it.
code: FROM signups AS s, __1__(s.meta, '__2__') AS t

steps.title: Tag popularity
prompt: Return each **tag** and the number of members who chose it (**members**), most popular first, ties broken by tag A to Z.
Tables: `signups(id, raw_name, email, phone, meta)`; `meta` is JSON text such as `{"source":"web","tags":["books"],"marketing":true}`.
solution: SELECT t.value AS tag, COUNT(*) AS members
FROM signups AS s, json_each(s.meta, '$.tags') AS t
setup: CREATE TABLE signups (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, raw_name TEXT, email TEXT, phone TEXT, meta TEXT);

steps.title: Proper names
prompt: Return **id** and **name**: `raw_name` trimmed, with the first letter **upper case** and the rest **lower case** (only the very first letter of the whole string, so `ana SOUSA` becomes `Ana sousa`), **only for members who agreed to marketing** (`"marketing": true` in the JSON, which SQLite returns as `1`).
Tables: `signups(id, raw_name, email, phone, meta)`; `meta` is JSON text such as `{"source":"web","tags":["books"],"marketing":true}`.
solution: SELECT id, UPPER(substr(TRIM(raw_name), 1, 1)) || LOWER(substr(TRIM(raw_name), 2)) AS name
